Control Name: Enforce SSH key-based authentication (disable password login)
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Quick to configure and blocks the most common brute-force attack path on Linux servers.

Control Name: Restrict or disable direct root SSH login
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: One config change removes a high-value attack target with almost no operational cost.

Control Name: Enable multi-factor authentication for the cloud provider console
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Stops most account-takeover attacks even if a password is leaked; low effort with big payoff.

Control Name: Limit sudo privileges using role-based access
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Reduces blast radius if one account is compromised; simple to set up for a small team.

Control Name: Rotate cloud API keys and secrets on a schedule
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Limits how long a leaked credential stays useful to an attacker.

Control Name: Enable automatic OS security updates
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Closes known vulnerabilities automatically without needing dedicated staff time.

Control Name: Maintain a patch schedule for third-party software and dependencies
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Covers the gap left by OS auto-updates, which often skip application-level packages.

Control Name: Configure a host-based firewall (ufw/firewalld)
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Blocks unnecessary inbound traffic with a short, one-time setup.

Control Name: Apply least-privilege security group / network rules
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Shrinks the attack surface by only opening ports that are actually needed.

Control Name: Enforce TLS for all web-facing services
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Protects data in transit; most cloud load balancers make this low effort to enable.

Control Name: Enable fail2ban or similar brute-force protection
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Automatically blocks repeated failed login attempts with minimal ongoing maintenance.

Control Name: Enable centralized logging (rsyslog / cloud logging service)
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Gives visibility into incidents after the fact; foundational for any later monitoring.

Control Name: Enable audit logging (auditd) on critical hosts
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Tracks privileged actions for investigation, required by many compliance baselines.

Control Name: Set up alerting for repeated failed login attempts
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Turns raw logs into an early warning system without needing a full SOC.

Control Name: Set up automated vulnerability scanning
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Surfaces known CVEs on a schedule so gaps don't rely on manual review.

Control Name: Enable disk encryption at rest
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Protects data if a disk or backup is stolen or improperly decommissioned.

Control Name: Configure regular encrypted backups with periodic restore tests
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Limits damage from ransomware or accidental deletion; often the single highest-value control.

Control Name: Remove unused packages, services, and default accounts
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Reduces the number of things that can be exploited, at essentially zero ongoing cost.

Control Name: Deploy basic intrusion detection (e.g., OSSEC)
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Adds detection capability for a small org without the cost of a full SIEM.

Control Name: Document and periodically test an incident response plan
Typical Benefit for Small Orgs: Cheap to create and dramatically shortens recovery time when something does go wrong.
